headline: Plastic was made to last. Most of it still is.

portrait.alt: Profile photograph of Leo Baekeland, balding, with a dark beard and a light jacket
portrait.credit: Leo Baekeland, 1916. The World's Work. Public domain.

slides.label: The bright idea
slides.title: Bugs can't keep up
slides.text: The US was going electric, and a common insulator, shellac, came from lac insects in limited supply. **Leo Baekeland set out to make a substitute.**

slides.label: It worked
slides.title: Heat, pressure, Bakelite
slides.text: In 1907 he made Bakelite, the first fully synthetic plastic, and announced it in 1909. **Soon it was in car parts, radios and telephones.**

slides.label: The backfire
slides.title: Made to last, so it does
slides.statLabel: of plastic waste by 2015 sat in landfills or nature, one study says
slides.text: Most plastics after Bakelite don't biodegrade in any meaningful sense, a study author says. **Most plastic waste is still around.**

slides.label: Could anyone have seen it coming?
slides.title: Not in his lifetime
slides.text: In 1950 the world made about 2 million metric tons of plastic a year, and ocean plastic was first noticed in the 1960s. **Nothing in 1907 pointed here.**

slides.label: The long cleanup
slides.title: Still negotiating
slides.text: In 2022, 175 nations agreed to write a treaty to end plastic pollution. Talks in 2024 and 2025 ended without a deal. **The treaty is still unwritten.**

slides.label: The ledger
slides.title: Worth it?
gains: Insulation without waiting on lac insects
Molded parts for cars, radios and telephones
Over 400 million metric tons of plastic made in 2015
costs: 79% of 6.3 billion metric tons of plastic waste in landfills or nature by 2015 (Science Advances, 2017)
Plastic particles in the blood of 17 of 22 donors in one 2022 study
A plastics treaty still unwritten after talks in 2024 and 2025
slides.text: It gave an electric country its insulators and a material made at over 400 million tons a year. **It cost billions of tons of waste that lingers.**

slides.label: Pattern
slides.title: Too stable to go away
slides.text: Bakelite sold because heat could not melt it and solvents could not dissolve it. **The same toughness keeps plastic on beaches for decades.**

slides.label: Lesson
slides.title: What we take from it
slides.text: How long a thing lasts and how long it stays useful are different numbers. **Plan for where it goes after its job.**
